ui.foot: {i} of {n}. Schools can pick any topics, in any order.

list.d: Using basic hand tools safely and handling the small fixes every home needs.
L: What each common hand tool is for, and how to hold it.
Tighten a loose handle, hang something level, change a light bulb.
Find the shutoff valve and what to do first during a leak.
list.st: A practice board with screws, nails, a level and a shutoff valve.
list.stop: Breakers, wiring, gas or anything sparking: step back and get an adult or a professional.

list.d: Troubleshooting devices, protecting accounts and spotting scams before they cost you.
L: A simple routine that fixes most device problems.
Passphrases, two-step sign-in and never sharing a password.
The red flags in fake prizes, account alerts and “new number” texts.
list.st: Sample messages and a practice account to secure.
list.stop: Money lost, threats, or someone pressuring you to keep secrets: tell a trusted adult right away.

list.d: Daily routines and doing laundry from start to finish.
L: What wash and dry symbols mean.
Sort, measure, wash, dry and fold.
list.st: A sorting station with real clothes and care labels.
list.stop: Ask before using bleach or other strong cleaning products.

list.d: Kitchen safety, following a recipe, making a simple meal, and cleaning up.
L: Handwashing, a clean surface and safe knife handling.
Measuring, timing and following steps in order.
A no-stove meal, then cleanup as part of cooking.
list.st: Recipe cards, measuring tools and no-stove ingredients.
list.stop: Stovetops and ovens come later, with an adult always present.

list.d: Needs versus wants, comparing prices and building the habit of saving a little.
L: Sorting real purchases and deciding what comes first.
Unit prices, sales and when cheaper isn’t better.
A simple plan for spending, and setting some aside.
list.st: A mock store with price tags and a weekly budget.
list.stop: Anyone asking for card numbers, passwords or gift cards: stop and check with an adult.

list.d: Introducing yourself, making a call and disagreeing respectfully.
L: A handshake, eye contact and a clear introduction.
Planning what to say, then calling to ask or reschedule.
Staying calm and respectful when you don’t agree.
list.stop: Any conversation that feels unsafe: walk away and find a trusted adult.

list.d: Recognizing when a job is too big or unsafe, and knowing exactly who to ask.
L: Sorting situations by who should handle them.
Naming the adults you can go to at home, school and nearby.
When to leave, when to call 911, and what to say.
list.st: Scenario cards drawn from real household situations.
list.stop: This one is part of every other topic too.

list.d: For older students, later on: dashboard lights, tire checks, and what to do if a car breaks down.
L: Checking pressure and tread, with an adult.
list.stop: All vehicle work happens with an adult. Nothing under the hood without one.
